system_description.narrative_title: Global bond-market sell-off and rising yields stressing policy
system_description.narrative_summary: An interconnected surge in sovereign bond yields — driven by oil-led inflation fears, hawkish central-bank moves and a disappointing U.S. Treasury buyback — is reshaping investor positioning and testing monetary and fiscal tools. As an open system, the fixed-income market continuously exchanges information, capital and expectations with external drivers (commodity shocks, geopolitics) and policy agents (central banks, treasuries), producing feedback loops (yields ↔ policy ↔ risk appetite) that amplify shocks and force adjustments across asset classes.
system_description.scope: The global fixed-income complex (sovereign yields, credit spreads, repo and wholesale funding), central-bank and treasury policy responses, investor flow dynamics (hedge funds, insurers, asset managers), and near-term inflation drivers (notably energy prices).
system_description.super_system: The global macro-financial system (real economy, cross-border capital flows, and monetary–fiscal interactions).
adjacent_subsystems: Energy and commodity markets (oil prices, geopolitics)
Sovereign fiscal and debt-management operations (issuance, buybacks)
Equities and corporate credit / private credit markets
FX and safe-haven assets (gold, currencies, capital flight)

variables.name: Long-term bond yield level
variables.description: The average yield level on long-dated sovereign bonds across markets, reflecting compensation for carrying duration risk.

variables.name: Credit spread level
variables.description: The average premium demanded by investors for holding non-government debt versus sovereign benchmarks across credit qualities.

variables.name: Term premium
variables.description: The component of long-term yields that compensates investors for interest-rate risk and uncertainty beyond expected short rates.

variables.name: Repo market liquidity
variables.description: The available depth and ease of collateralized short-term funding in the secured lending (repo) market.

variables.name: Wholesale funding costs
variables.description: The average cost of unsecured and secured short- to medium-term financing for financial intermediaries in wholesale markets.

variables.name: Net government bond supply
variables.description: The net flow of government debt issuance minus buybacks and maturities over a given period, representing the market's new supply shock.

variables.name: Policy interest rate level
variables.description: The prevailing short-term policy interest rate that anchors monetary conditions and short-term money market rates.

variables.name: Policy rate expectations
variables.description: Market participants' collective expectations about the future path of policy interest rates over the forecast horizon.

variables.name: Realized inflation rate
variables.description: Observed rates of consumer or producer price inflation over a recent period, capturing actual price-level changes.

variables.name: Energy price level
variables.description: The prevailing price index for energy commodities (notably oil and gas) that transmits to broader inflation and production costs.

variables.name: Inflation expectations
variables.description: The medium-term expected inflation rate embedded in surveys, market pricing and long-term contracts.

variables.name: Investor risk appetite
variables.description: A composite measure of investors' willingness to hold riskier assets versus safe assets, reflecting demand for carry and credit exposure.

variables.name: Cross-border capital flows
variables.description: Net portfolio and debt flows across countries that redistribute global funding and demand for fixed-income securities.

variables.name: Investor leverage ratio
variables.description: The average leverage—debt relative to equity or assets—employed by leveraged financial investors across markets.

variables.name: Market volatility level
variables.description: The prevailing level of price volatility and uncertainty priced into derivatives and observed in realized returns across fixed-income markets.

variables.name: Average duration exposure
variables.description: The weighted-average interest-rate duration held by market participants, indicating sensitivity of portfolios to yield moves.

catalysts.title: Fed policy decision (mid‑Sept)
catalysts.description: FOMC decision on policy rates and statement likely in the coming week, with markets pricing a hike if inflation prints stay hot.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Week Ahead... All Eyes on Fed Rate Decision'; 'Fed rate-hike case builds' — hot data could push Fed to hike.

catalysts.title: BOJ rate rise expected next week
catalysts.description: Bank of Japan is poised to lift policy rates in the next week, shifting global rate differentials and safe‑haven flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'BOJ to raise rates to 1.25% this month' and 'BOJ set to lift rates next week' — expected tightening in Japan.

catalysts.title: US inflation prints (PPI/CPI) due
catalysts.description: Near‑term U.S. inflation data releases (PPI/CPI) will inform Fed decisions and market rate pricing.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Gold Rises... Fed Policy in Focus'; 'Hot inflation data sets up a Fed rate hike' — prints will move policy pricing.

catalysts.title: Sustained oil price surge
catalysts.description: Recent jumps in oil (to ~$107–109) amid Middle East tensions could persist, raising inflationary pressures and bond yields.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Global bond sell-off reignites as oil jumps to $109'; 'ECB to hike as Iran war fuels fresh inflation fears'.

catalysts.title: Risk of further ECB hikes in October
catalysts.description: Markets put a meaningful probability on another ECB rate increase in October as energy risks and inflation concerns persist.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Markets see a near 50-50 chance the ECB will hike again in October'; 'ECB policymakers open door to more rate hikes.'

catalysts.title: Follow‑on US Treasury buyback operations
catalysts.description: After a $6bn buyback that disappointed markets, continued or expanded Treasury buybacks are likely to be debated and possibly executed.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'U.S. Treasury Plans $6 Billion Buyback'; 'Bessent’s buyback fails to calm market' — follow-ons considered.

catalysts.title: Portfolio rebalancing / de‑risking flows
catalysts.description: Investors are rebalancing as bond yields climb and stocks rally, likely prompting duration cuts, leverage reduction and volatile flows over coming weeks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Bond sell-off, stock boom: Why rebalancing is a good strategy'; 'Bonds have become bonds again' — de-risking flows likely.

catalysts.title: European fiscal borrowing pressure (Q4)
catalysts.description: Rising interest bills (eg France) and fiscal strains could increase government issuance in coming months, pressuring yields and spreads.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'France’s debt interest bill to jump 25% this year' — fiscal pressure implies higher issuance and funding needs.
